collection.description: A dry cough has gone through the children, and now three adults have it too, and the healers are run off their feet.

ask.text:
A dry cough has gone through the children, and now three adults have it too, and the healers are run off their feet. (Name), who helps them, has an idea: the old healers used to build a steam hut over a hot spring, and the sick would sit in it, all together. Or (name) could go hut to hut with the usual honey and leaf tea, which is slower but gets to everyone.
What should (name) do?

c1o1.text: After three days of sitting in the steam, the coughs are loose and fading. The healers learn a great deal about which leaves to put on the hot stones, and argue about it cheerfully. The steam hut stays, and becomes everyone's favourite place on a cold evening.

c1o2.text: The steam is too much for some of them. One elder faints, and the healers have to drag people out into the cool air. The coughs get better in the end, slowly, the ordinary way. The steam hut is taken down, and (name) is teased about it for a month.

c1.text: (Name) and the healers build a little hut of woven leaves over the hot spring in a single day, and fill it with the sick, coughing and grumbling and sweating...

c2o1.text: It takes two weeks, and (name) barely sleeps, but by the end the cough is gone from every hut. The children call (name) "the honey one," and run to (him/her) whenever they see (him/her) coming, in case there's honey left.

c2o2.text: (Name) has always been squeamish around the sick, and only helped the healers by carrying things. But two weeks of sitting with coughing children changes that. By the end, (he/she) isn't squeamish at all, and asks the healers to teach (him/her) properly. The cough passes, in its own time.

c2.text: (Name) goes from hut to hut with a pot of honey and a basket of leaves, day after day, making tea and sitting with the sick...
